forecast.method: Seasonal naive (same month last year) x year-to-date growth on matching months; band = 2 x std of the log errors of earlier months only (±25% until 3 months are known)

summary.overview: We tested 100% of the ledger (102,429 entries, 643 manual). 3,094 entries reached a risk score of 50 or more, worth 4,122,399 EUR under review (not a loss estimate). Ground truth (dataset): 832 of 850 labelled entries are alerted.
key_themes: Timing (when it was posted or entered): 2205 alerts
Flagged by the models only: 605 alerts
recommended_next_steps: Review the High alerts first and obtain the evidence listed in each memo
Discuss late and weekend postings with the chief accountant
Check the users and bank accounts behind cash and clearing alerts
Extend the test to the next closing period
limitations: Risk scores prioritise audit attention; they are not probabilities of fraud
The ledger and its labels are synthetic: real fraud may look different
Thresholds and materiality are our assumptions
Template text - run the local LLM for a written summary

log: v1 - auditor persona, JSON output, French audit vocabulary (FEC/PCG sample data).
v2 - adapted to the DIB general ledger (SKR03 accounts, entry timestamps, users); memo uses the rules triggered and the SHAP drivers; added the assertion at risk and the NEP 240 / ISA 240 link.

v3 - merged Person 3's safeguards (no fraud claims, distinguish facts / scores / indicators / items to verify, leave the auditor's conclusion blank); memo grounded in Person 3's recommendation library; added the 'ask the alerts' prompt for natural-language questions.

library.name: System - auditor persona
library.text:
You are an audit documentation assistant supporting a human external auditor
applying NEP 240 / ISA 240 (testing the appropriateness of journal entries and other adjustments).

Strict rules:
- Use ONLY the facts and audit recommendations supplied in the user message.
  Never invent dates, amounts, account names, approvals, documents, explanations or evidence.
- Do not claim or imply that fraud, theft, misconduct or management override occurred.
- Distinguish clearly between (1) facts in the ledger, (2) model screening scores,
  (3) rule-based indicators and (4) matters that still require auditor verification.
- A risk score is a prioritisation indicator, NOT a probability of fraud and NOT proof.
  Do not change, reinterpret or recalculate it.
- If no driver is identified, say that the specific driver is not identified.
- Neutral, concise, professional audit language. Write in {language}.
- Leave the auditor's conclusion and sign-off for human completion.
- Answer ONLY with valid JSON, no text before or after.

recommendation_library.potential_risk: Potential material misstatement or unsupported estimate; unusual size may warrant override testing.
recommendation_library.evidence_to_request: Invoice or contract; purchase order; goods receipt or service acceptance; approval evidence; calculation supporting the amount.
recommendation_library.audit_procedure: Agree amount to source documents and contract; assess business purpose and authorisation; compare with similar transactions and materiality.
recommendation_library.scope_note: High amount is a dataset scenario, not proof of error or fraud.

recommendation_library.potential_risk: Potential unsupported cash payment or misappropriation risk, particularly where cash controls are weak.
recommendation_library.evidence_to_request: Cash voucher; receipt or invoice; petty-cash log; payment record; approval; reconciliation.
recommendation_library.audit_procedure: Trace disbursement to evidence; verify recipient and business purpose; inspect approval and cash reconciliation.
recommendation_library.scope_note: Do not infer missing approval unless records are inspected.

recommendation_library.potential_risk: Potential cut-off error or delayed recording.
recommendation_library.evidence_to_request: Source invoice; goods receipt/service date; posting record; explanation for delay.
recommendation_library.audit_procedure: Compare document, posting and entry dates; assess correct accounting period and cut-off impact.
recommendation_library.scope_note: Dataset threshold is 10–29 days; check available date fields.

recommendation_library.potential_risk: Potential cut-off misstatement or late recognition; possible override requires corroboration.
recommendation_library.evidence_to_request: Source invoice; contract; goods receipt/service evidence; posting record; subsequent payment or reversal; explanation.
recommendation_library.audit_procedure: Reconstruct timeline; assess accounting period; inspect settlement/reversal; evaluate whether adjustment or expanded testing is needed.
recommendation_library.scope_note: More than 29 days in the dataset; delay alone does not prove concealment.

recommendation_library.potential_risk: Unusual posting activity; possible exceptional processing or weak review controls.
recommendation_library.evidence_to_request: Entry timestamp; user activity log; approval trail if maintained; source document; access log.
recommendation_library.audit_procedure: Confirm actual time and user; compare with entity procedures; inspect authorisation and support.
recommendation_library.scope_note: Does not establish manual or unauthorised posting.

recommendation_library.potential_risk: Unusual posting timing; possible exceptional processing.
recommendation_library.evidence_to_request: Entry timestamp; user activity log; approval trail; source document; explanation for weekend processing.
recommendation_library.audit_procedure: Verify date/time; establish whether weekend processing is normal; inspect approval and support.

recommendation_library.potential_risk: Potential use of an unapproved bank account or misdirected funds.
recommendation_library.evidence_to_request: Bank account master data; bank statement/confirmation; payment instruction; vendor/customer master change log; approval.
recommendation_library.audit_procedure: Verify account against authorised bank records; trace to bank evidence; inspect creation/change history and approval.
recommendation_library.scope_note: Must be independently verified; never infer from account code alone.

recommendation_library.potential_risk: Potential unusual clearing relationship, misallocation or concealment of an open balance.
recommendation_library.evidence_to_request: Invoices; credit notes; clearing documents; subledger; counterparty confirmation; reconciliation.
recommendation_library.audit_procedure: Reconstruct the clearing chain; match amounts/dates/counterparties; inspect rationale and supporting documents.
recommendation_library.scope_note: Cross-linking is not automatically a duplicate or misstatement.

recommendation_library.potential_risk: Possible duplicate recording or repeated reference requiring investigation.
recommendation_library.evidence_to_request: Source documents; invoice numbers; vendor/customer details; reversal records.
recommendation_library.audit_procedure: Search exact and near-duplicate references; compare amounts, dates, counterparties and reversal history.
recommendation_library.scope_note: Use only if duplicate-reference detection is independently implemented.

recommendation_library.potential_risk: Possible misclassification or unexpected posting pattern.
recommendation_library.evidence_to_request: Chart of accounts; accounting policy; source documents; comparable prior entries.
recommendation_library.audit_procedure: Compare account combination with approved posting logic and similar transactions; inspect business rationale.
recommendation_library.scope_note: Do not infer incorrect coding from an unfamiliar account signature alone.

recommendation_library.potential_risk: Possible inappropriate access or segregation-of-duties concern.
recommendation_library.evidence_to_request: User access matrix; activity logs; role/approval matrix; change logs.
recommendation_library.audit_procedure: Compare activity with user role and historical baseline; inspect access rights and independent approval.
recommendation_library.scope_note: User identity alone does not establish authorisation or wrongdoing.

recommendation_library.potential_risk: Potential inability to substantiate occurrence, accuracy or business purpose.
recommendation_library.evidence_to_request: Invoice/contract; purchase order; delivery/service evidence; payment proof; approval trail.
recommendation_library.audit_procedure: Request documents and inspect completeness; if unavailable, document limitation and perform alternatives.
recommendation_library.scope_note: Cannot be concluded from ledger data alone; requires document inspection.

recommendation_library.potential_risk: Potential override of established controls or accounting estimates.
recommendation_library.evidence_to_request: Journal approval trail; access logs; estimate support; board/audit committee records; source documents.
recommendation_library.audit_procedure: Inspect unusual manual journals, approval exceptions and estimate changes; corroborate with independent evidence.
recommendation_library.scope_note: Requires additional evidence; never infer override from a high score alone.

generic_recommendation.anomaly: Model-prioritised entry; specific driver not identified
generic_recommendation.potential_risk: The entry may warrant further review due to its model score. The score alone does not establish an error, irregularity or fraud.
generic_recommendation.evidence_to_request: Obtain the source invoice/contract, evidence of delivery or service, payment evidence, approval trail and relevant correspondence.
generic_recommendation.audit_procedure: Agree the entry to source documentation; verify business purpose, authorisation, amount, accounting period, account coding and settlement.
generic_recommendation.scope_note: General follow-up only. Do not attribute the score to a particular feature unless the model explanation supports it.
